P1.evidence: Warm personal open about the prospect's fishing trip with his sons. The frame was three-part, not four: 'for this call, I want to dive in really deep on where you're at, where we're trying to get to just figure out what's kind of been missing for us' — 'what you need' is absent. No frame agreement was sought; he went straight into 'Walk me through though, what do you feel we could potentially help you with?' Prior-call notes were read back, but mid-call rather than at the open: 'didn't you mention, I think I remember you mentioning you were trying to carry the kids up and you were like winded by the top of the stairs'.

P2.evidence: The strongest phase of the call and close to complete. 'how old are you, what's your height, and what's your weight?' (38, 6ft, 210); work plus the sedentary follow-up 'Is there a lot of sitting with work, though?'; injuries probed with duration; training week walked through in detail; physique and endurance progress both asked; diet interrogated down to calories and protein tracking; sleep quantity, quality and napping; energy through the day. P2c is partial only because hereditary conditions were never asked and the direct question 'any health conditions at all' drew a flat 'no' — the TRT only surfaced later when the rep asked about energy.

P3.evidence: The bridge to why was run cleanly — 'Why is all this important to you right now, do you feel?' — and landed the strongest material in the call: 'five and seven-year-old, they're sitting there looking up to me like I'm Superman, and I'm feeling like I'm Kingpin instead.' Goals were reflected and confirmed ('longevity, mobility, injury prevention, anything else's kind of primary goals?'). But he did not go on to work it: 'when you're moving better, what does that actually do for you?' and 'who else does that impact?' were never asked, and instead of driving through to identity and legacy he pivoted to the divorce story. The final reflection was surface-level — 'it's sounding like we're just wanting to bring this thing up to a next level' — not the 'this isn't really about the weight, it's about X' move.

P4.evidence: 'What else have we tried up to this point?' was asked and drew a thin answer. He asked what changed — 'what was it that actually shifted for you' — which produced the stairs moment, but never asked why the previous approach failed to stick. The gap was named by the prospect in one word, 'Accountability', in answer to 'why else do you feel like coaching might be a good fit for you'. The root-cause move — 'the information isn't the problem, why can't you stick to it on your own?' — was never run, which matters here because the prospect had already said he researches endlessly online.

P5.evidence: No consequence frame was built at all. The two-year question, the willingness-to-settle question and the 'why not' were all skipped. Only the closing move ran, and it ran cold, bundled into a summary: 'do you feel like we are really ready to draw a line in the sand with this stuff, or, like, how are we feeling?' The answer — 'I'm ready to get at it and do what I've got to do' — was accepted without the cost of inaction ever being made real.

P6.evidence: The sequence is inverted: the whole three-pillar presentation was delivered before any commitment check. The belief question came afterwards and in weakened form — 'do you feel between nutrition, training, accountability, that's everything that you need?' — though he did press on the soft answer, 'Think so or no? So what are we missing?', which is the right instinct. The all-in question was run properly: 'provided we can work out all the logistics... do you feel that, hey man, I really can commit to going all-in?' It returned a conditional yes about mountain biking days, which he resolved before moving to price.

P11.evidence: Onboarding was booked for 4:15pm the next day and details were taken. Payment was attempted but not collected: the prospect needs to liquidate precious metals, so the rep improvised a $100 holding deposit — 'Let's just do a super small deposit, even just $100 so we have something in' — which was itself only conditionally agreed. The agreement was mentioned as a future action ('I can get you the documentation all done up') and never confirmed as received or signed on the call. Nothing was said about the welcome email, the Skool link or the onboarding questionnaire; Skool appeared earlier only as a feature in the pillar pitch. The recording truncates at 00:35:37, so steps 3 and 4 are scored as not done by the cut.

objection_plays.detail: A liquidity trigger landed at 00:34:00 — 'I'm going to have to go and transfer some funds', then 'I invest a lot in precious metals and whatnot' — and no part of the money play was run. There was no isolation question, no 'should I versus how' reframe, and none of the financial picture: cash on hand, monthly surplus, cards, available credit, investments. Instead the rep skipped straight to a $100 token deposit. The play was arguably unnecessary given zero price resistance, but the outcome is that the deal now depends on the prospect selling physical gold unassisted, with nothing verified about his capacity to pay.

The prospect asked a direct terms question — 'Is that all one time? Is that monthly?' — and the script has no defined answer for it. The rep replied 'Most people just put out a credit card, do it at once', which is social proof rather than an answer, and instalment options were never named. This is a gap in the script, not a rep failure: there is no scripted disclosure for what a prospect is told when they ask outright how the $6,000 is paid.

A programme-fit condition was attached to the commitment — the prospect wants five kettlebell days plus two mountain biking days. Handled adequately and off-script with 'Trevor's super flexible, man... he'll just work around it', and the prospect moved on. No scripted play exists for a competing-activity condition.
No think-about-it trigger; the prospect agreed on the spot.
No partner-consult trigger; the prospect is single and has sole custody.
No timing objection; the prospect asked 'when do we start?' during the training pillar.
No fear or doubt raised about the programme.

notes: SCORING NOTE: the disposition here was corrected from closed to lost after the 07/09 team meeting revealed the prospect never paid and hung up on the follow-up. The phase scores below were assigned from the transcript alone, before that was known, and are unchanged — they describe what the rep did, not how it ended. Excellent baseline and a genuinely warm rapport, then the process thins out badly from Phase 5 onward — no consequence frame, a commitment check run after the presentation rather than before, and a close that depends on the prospect liquidating gold with no financial picture taken. The coachable point is that an easy yes was allowed to substitute for the work: the prospect said 'Sweet deal' at $6,000, so P5 was skipped and payment was never actually collected. Also worth correcting: a direct question about payment terms was answered with social proof instead of the terms.
